boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Harvard rituals spanning Housing Day celebrations, House customs, convocations, and centuries-old Commencement practices.

cards.title: Meet Your House on Housing Day
cards.subtitle: First-years receive their upper-level House assignments before spring break
cards.notes: Watch for costumed House teams in Harvard Yard, then follow your assigned House’s official instructions for its welcome events.
cards.short_summary: A spirited reveal turns Harvard’s residential assignment process into a campus-wide celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard identifies Housing Day as a notable College tradition when first-years learn their housing assignments for subsequent years during the week before spring break.
cards.access_notes: The tradition centers on current Harvard College first-years receiving House assignments; consult College announcements for current arrangements.

cards.title: Gather in the Yard for Yardfest
cards.subtitle: Harvard College’s April cookout and festival-style concert
cards.notes: Check the Dean of Students calendar for the date and entry rules, then look for the cookout and concert setup in Tercentenary Theatre.
cards.short_summary: An annual spring gathering brings the Harvard College community together for food and live music.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard’s Dean of Students Office says the entire Harvard College community gathers each April in Tercentenary Theatre for Yardfest, a giant cookout and festival-style concert.
cards.source_title: Harvard College Traditions | Harvard College Dean of Students Office
cards.access_notes: Described by Harvard as an event for the Harvard College community; verify the current date and access requirements with the Dean of Students Office.

cards.title: Process into First-Year Convocation
cards.subtitle: Class pins and a formal welcome before fall classes begin
cards.notes: Follow Opening Days instructions for the procession, keep your class pin, and listen for the history and values introduced during the ceremony.
cards.short_summary: Harvard welcomes each incoming class with alumni, a procession, and class pins.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard Alumni says First-Year Convocation began in 2009, continues annually, occurs the day before fall classes, and includes a procession and class-pin presentation.
cards.access_notes: Convocation is for incoming Harvard College first-years and participating alumni; follow official Opening Days guidance.

cards.title: Call Harvard–Yale Simply “The Game”
cards.subtitle: The Crimson and Bulldogs’ rivalry meeting, played since 1875
cards.notes: Confirm the year’s host campus and ticket policy before attending, then look for the event identified in Harvard materials simply as “The Game.”
cards.short_summary: Harvard’s long-running football rivalry with Yale carries a deliberately spare name.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard College documents that the Harvard Crimson and Yale Bulldogs have met since 1875 in an event known simply as “The Game.”
cards.access_notes: Attendance and location vary by year; consult Harvard Athletics for the current schedule and ticket requirements.

cards.entity_name: Pforzheimer House International Polar Bear Day
cards.title: Mark Polar Bear Day at Pfoho
cards.subtitle: A House observance that includes adopting a wild polar bear
cards.notes: Look for Pforzheimer House’s official event notice before participating and use the documented conservation activity as the focal point.
cards.short_summary: Pforzheimer House gives an international observance a distinctly Harvard House expression.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard College lists Pforzheimer House’s annual International Polar Bear Day celebration as a House tradition and says it includes adopting a real polar bear in the wild.
cards.access_notes: This is a Pforzheimer House tradition; participation details are determined by the House and should be checked with its staff.

cards.title: Pause for Lowell Tea
cards.subtitle: A recurring custom named among Harvard’s House traditions
cards.notes: Consult Lowell House’s current calendar before going, and follow any resident or guest-access instructions attached to the gathering.
cards.short_summary: A named tea gathering represents the smaller traditions cultivated inside Harvard’s House system.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard College specifically identifies the much-anticipated Lowell Tea as one of the traditions embraced by students in the Houses.
cards.access_notes: Harvard’s overview does not specify a current schedule or public access; check directly with Lowell House.

cards.title: Dress for the First-Year Formal
cards.subtitle: A class-specific event in Harvard College’s tradition cycle
cards.notes: Wait for official first-year programming details before making plans, then follow the announced attire, location, and access guidance.
cards.short_summary: The incoming class gets a formal gathering of its own within Harvard’s annual student traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard College names the First-Year Formal alongside Housing Day and Yardfest as an experience that immerses students in College history and campus life.
cards.access_notes: The official traditions overview does not provide current scheduling or eligibility details; follow Harvard College first-year announcements.

cards.title: Join Harvard’s Oldest Tradition
cards.subtitle: A University ceremony traced to nine graduates in September 1642
cards.notes: Use the Commencement Office schedule to distinguish the University exercises from the later House and School diploma ceremonies.
cards.short_summary: Harvard’s oldest tradition joins a University-wide ceremony with smaller diploma presentations.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard College dates its first Commencement to September 1642 with nine seniors and describes the modern sequence of morning exercises followed by House and School diploma ceremonies.
cards.access_notes: Harvard Yard admission on Commencement morning is controlled, and guests require tickets; consult the Commencement Office for current policies.

cards.title: Open Commencement in Latin
cards.subtitle: A graduating senior delivers the first student oration from memory
cards.notes: Listen at the opening of the University exercises for the Latin address, one of three speeches selected through Harvard’s competition.
cards.short_summary: A memorized Latin greeting preserves an unusually old component of Harvard Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard’s Commencement Office calls the Student Orations Competition one of its oldest traditions and states that its first oration is delivered in Latin by a graduating College senior.
cards.access_notes: The oration is part of the ticketed Commencement exercises; competition eligibility and submission rules apply to prospective speakers.

cards.title: Sing Psalm 78 to St. Martin’s
cards.subtitle: A Harvard ceremonial pairing documented since at least 1806
cards.notes: Use the current Baccalaureate program to follow the service and listen for Psalm 78 set to the historic St. Martin’s tune.
cards.short_summary: One specific psalm-and-tune pairing links today’s senior ceremony to two centuries of Harvard observance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Memorial Church says Psalm 78 set to St. Martin’s has been sung at Harvard Commencement and Baccalaureate since at least 1806 and remains a symbol of continuity.
cards.source_title: Harvard College Baccalaureate 2026 | The Memorial Church
cards.access_notes: Baccalaureate arrangements and audience access are set annually; consult the current Memorial Church and Commencement guidance.
